9c4e43be.t:
Two magnets meet.
One asks: "What should I wear (in German: anziehen) today?"
9c4e43be.why: "Anziehen" has two meanings: to put on clothes – and a magnet attracts (pulls/draws) metal.

052104b5.t:
Teacher: "Little Fritz, name three animals from Africa!"
Little Fritz: "Two lions and an elephant."
052104b5.why: The teacher means three different species of animals. Little Fritz simply counts three individual animals.

ce31f5d2.t:
What is a cookie under a tree?
A shady spot (in German: Plätzchen).
ce31f5d2.why: "Plätzchen" means a little cookie – and also a small spot/place. Under a tree, there is shade.

0e56c03b.t:
Announcement on the train: "Our train is on time today."
All passengers get off: "This must be the wrong train!"
0e56c03b.why: In Germany, trains are often delayed. An on-time train is so unusual that nobody believes it.

aaad3f46.t:
Guest: "Waiter, what is this fly doing in my soup?"
Waiter: "I think it's doing backstroke."
aaad3f46.why: The guest is complaining. The waiter takes the question literally and describes what the fly is currently "doing".

95942fbb.t:
What is brown, sticky, and walks through the desert?
A caram-el (in German: Karamel).
95942fbb.why: Caramel is brown and sticky. The German word "Kamel" (camel) is hidden inside the word "Karamell" – and camels walk through the desert.

7db0d9d2.t:
In German class: "Is it der, die, or das Butter?"
Student: "Doesn't matter – as long as it's on the bread!"
7db0d9d2.why: Articles in German are hard. The student doesn't care – he just wants to eat. (The correct form is: die Butter.)

579755b5.t:
Two fish meet.
One says: "Hi!"
The other cries: "Where?!"
579755b5.why: "Hi" sounds like the German word "Hai" (shark). A shark is a dangerous fish – that's why the other fish gets scared.

63451d36.t:
Little Fritz: "Dad, can you write in the dark?"
Dad: "Yes, why?"
Little Fritz: "Then please turn off the light and sign my report card."
63451d36.why: The report card is bad. Dad is supposed to sign it without seeing the grades.

9b5ed458.t:
What lies on the beach and mumbles?
A mumble-shell (in German: Nuschel).
9b5ed458.why: "Nuscheln" means to mumble. Seashells ("Muscheln") lie on the beach. Muschel + nuscheln = Nuschel.

16787b36.t:
What do you call a boomerang that doesn't come back?
A stick.
16787b36.why: A boomerang flies back. If it doesn't, it is just a piece of wood – a stick.

feaa04eb.t:
"I would like to make an appointment at the citizens' office."
"The next available appointment is in March."
"Great. And in which year?"
feaa04eb.why: In Germany, waiting times for government office appointments are often very long. The man is already anticipating a wait of over a year.

b403ee2c.t:
What is orange and hikes through the mountains?
A hiking mandarin (in German: Wanderine).
b403ee2c.why: Mandarine (tangerine/mandarin, an orange fruit) + "wandern" (to hike) = Wanderine.

d864b375.t:
What do you call a sheep without legs?
A cloud.
d864b375.why: A sheep is white and fluffy. Without legs, it looks like a cloud in the sky.

9d72ed1d.t:
Teacher: "Can someone be punished for something they didn't do?"
Little Fritz: "No?"
Teacher: "Correct."
Little Fritz: "Good. I didn't do my homework."
9d72ed1d.why: Little Fritz cleverly exploits the rule: you can't be punished for something you didn't do—including not doing your homework.

319b0ecd.t:
What does a pirate do at the computer?
He presses the Enter key.
319b0ecd.why: Pirates "board" ships, which in German is "entern". "Enter" sounds exactly the same.

ac141760.t:
What does the zero say to the eight?
"Nice belt!"
ac141760.why: The number 8 looks like a 0 wearing a belt around the middle.

56b831a1.t:
Which bus traveled across the Atlantic?
Columbus (in German: Kolumbus).
56b831a1.why: Christopher Columbus sailed across the Atlantic to America. In German, his name ends with "-bus" ("Kolumbus").

31d2d76b.t:
Patient: "Doctor, lately I've been forgetting everything!"
Doctor: "How long have you had this?"
Patient: "Had what?"
31d2d76b.why: The patient has already forgotten what he was just talking about.

8bade9ed.t:
What is green and knocks on the door?
A knock-salad (in German: Klopfsalat).
8bade9ed.why: "Kopfsalat" (head of lettuce) is green. Adding an "l" turns it into "Klopf-salat"—and "klopfen" means to knock.

1debac24.t:
Waiter: "How did you find the steak?"
Guest: "Quite by accident—underneath a potato."
1debac24.why: "Wie finden Sie ...?" usually means "How do you like it?" (How is it?). The guest interprets "finden" literally as locating/discovering it—implying the steak was tiny.

dbd5b475.t:
Two toothpicks are walking through the forest.
A hedgehog passes by.
One of them says: "I had no idea a bus ran here!"
dbd5b475.why: To toothpicks, a hedgehog with all its spines looks like a bus packed full of fellow toothpicks.

8564507c.t:
"Doctor, I keep hearing a ringing in my ear!"
"Well, why don't you answer it?"
8564507c.why: When a phone rings, you "answer" it (in German: "rangehen"). The doctor pretends there is an actual telephone inside the ear.

445475a1.t:
What does a mathematician do in the garden?
They extract roots (in German: Wurzeln ziehen).
445475a1.why: In the garden, you pull roots ("Wurzeln ziehen") out of the ground. In math, calculating the square root of a number is also called "die Wurzel ziehen" (√9 = 3).

6f4350fa.t:
Where do cats like to live most?
In an apartment building (in German: Miezhaus).
6f4350fa.why: "Mieze" is an affectionate German word for a cat. A "Mietshaus" is an apartment building for rent, and both words sound almost identical.

9f944afb.t:
What is worse than finding a worm in your apple?
Finding half a worm in your apple.
9f944afb.why: If there is only half a worm left, you have already eaten the other half...

67ee40b1.t:
Boss: "How many people work in your department?"
Employee: "About half of them."
67ee40b1.why: The boss means: How many people are employed in the department? The answer implies: Only half of them actually work.

7b1421e3.t:
What is red and bad for your teeth?
A brick.
7b1421e3.why: You expect something like candy. But a brick is red—and very bad for your teeth if it hits you.

9d3f578b.t:
What does the big pencil say to the little pencil?
"Grow up, little one!" (in German: "Wachs mal, Stift!")
9d3f578b.why: A "Wachsmalstift" is a crayon. "Wachs mal!" sounds like "Wachse mal!"—meaning: Grow bigger already! At the same time, "Stift" is an informal German word for an apprentice.

6c092e2b.t:
What is the opposite of a health food store (in German: "Reformhaus")?
A deer behind the house (in German: "Reh hinterm Haus").
6c092e2b.why: "Reformhaus" sounds like "Reh vorm Haus" (deer in front of the house). The opposite of "vor" (in front of) is "hinter" (behind).

8e87fcb2.t:
What is a cowboy without a horse?
A semi-truck / saddle hauler (in German: "Sattelschlepper").
8e87fcb2.why: Without a horse, the cowboy has to drag/carry ("schleppen") his saddle ("Sattel") himself. A "Sattelschlepper" is actually a semi-trailer truck.

a9b4027e.t:
Teacher: "What is the plural of 'tree'?"
Little Fritz: "Forest!"
a9b4027e.why: The correct answer is "Bäume" (trees). Little Fritz thinks: Many trees together make a forest.

339fd042.t:
Why are ghosts so bad at lying?
Because you can see right through them (in German: "sie durchschauen").
339fd042.why: "Jemanden durchschauen" means to see through someone / realize that they are lying. But you can also literally look through a ghost.

faa71ba1.t:
What is white and disturbs your meal?
An avalanche.
faa71ba1.why: You expect something small, like spilled salt. But an avalanche (lots of snow) certainly disrupts a meal.

9300a2a2.t:
What is green and runs through the forest?
A herd of cucumbers.
9300a2a2.why: A nonsensical joke: Cucumbers are green, but they don't run in herds. That absurdity is what makes it funny.

61bab7c5.t:
Dad: "Do you know what an optimist is?"
Son: "No."
Dad: "Someone who solves a crossword puzzle with a ballpoint pen."
61bab7c5.why: With a ballpoint pen, you cannot erase mistakes. An optimist believes they won't make any mistakes.

16ec9c44.t:
Little Fritz arrives late to school.
Teacher: "Why are you late?"
Little Fritz: "The sign said: School – drive slowly!"
16ec9c44.why: The traffic sign is meant for car drivers. Little Fritz pretends he had to follow it on his way to school.

ded4531f.t:
What does a clown do in the office?
Sends faxes / fools around (in German: "Faxen").
ded4531f.why: "Faxe schicken" means sending faxes in an office. "Faxen machen" is an idiom meaning to fool around or clown around.

8cc9bced.t:
Two cows meet in a pasture.
One says: "Moo!"
The other says: "That's exactly what I was about to say!"
8cc9bced.why: Cows only ever say "Moo"—so they couldn't possibly say anything else anyway.

0a6932f4.t:
Why did the man throw his alarm clock out the window?
He wanted to see time fly (in German: wie die Zeit verfliegt).
0a6932f4.why: „Die Zeit verfliegt“ means time passes quickly. But here, the alarm clock is literally flying through the air.

7d6d8780.t:
Doctor: “You need to exercise more.”
Patient: “But I play soccer every day!”
Doctor: “Really?”
Patient: “Yes – on my game console.”
7d6d8780.why: The patient only plays soccer as a video game – while sitting on the couch.

7b42b6a1.t:
What is yellow and can't swim?
An excavator.
And why not?
It only has one arm.
7b42b6a1.why: A nonsensical joke: Excavators are often yellow and have an „Arm“ (boom/arm). The funny part is pretending that this is the reason it can't swim.

0d464845.t:
Teacher: “How many articles are there in German?”
Student: “Too many!”
0d464845.why: There are three: der, die, das. But to learners, it often feels like way more.

4c8f96d7.t:
Grandpa: “I'm cooking all by myself for the first time today.”
Grandson: “Okay. Where is the fire extinguisher?”
4c8f96d7.why: The grandson doesn't believe Grandpa can cook – he is already expecting a fire in the kitchen.

c671e1e2.t:
What is black and white and can't get through a revolving door?
A penguin on skis.
c671e1e2.why: A nonsensical joke: With long skis, you can't fit through a revolving door – not even as a penguin.

17195e50.t:
The teacher asks: “When I say ‘I am pretty’ – which tense is that?”
Little Fritz: “Past tense!”
17195e50.why: The correct answer is present tense (Präsens). Little Fritz cheekily implies she used to be pretty once in the past.

bb7c569a.t:
Customer at the bakery: “Is this bread from today?”
Baker: “No, from tomorrow – we're very early!”
bb7c569a.why: The customer wants fresh bread. The baker exaggerates: it is so fresh that it is already from tomorrow.

22030100.t:
Why do golfers bring two pairs of pants?
In case they get a hole in one (in German: ein Loch in einer haben).
22030100.why: In golf, you try to hit the ball into a „Loch“ (hole, as in a hole in one). A „Loch in der Hose“ (hole in your pants) is something completely different.

8460aa35.t:
I was going to tell a joke about the post office today.
But I don't know if it will deliver (in German: ob er ankommt).
8460aa35.why: „Ein Witz kommt an“ means people find it funny / it lands well. A letter „kommt an“ when it gets delivered successfully.

9cb522e3.t:
What do cows drink?
Milk? Wrong – water!
9cb522e3.why: Cows produce milk – but they drink water. Almost everyone answers incorrectly at first.

13c4ed70.t:
“Why are you sitting in front of the fridge with a flashlight?”
“I want to know if the light really goes out when the door is closed.”
13c4ed70.why: Almost everyone has wondered about this at some point – just usually people don't test it quite like that.

7bbd8047.t:
What does an itchy cloud do?
It flies to a skyscraper (in German: Wolkenkratzer).
7bbd8047.why: A „Wolkenkratzer“ (literally: cloud scratcher) is a skyscraper. A cloud that itches can scratch itself there, because „kratzen“ means to scratch.
